## 5. Certification Report (AMP600)
The report contains summary statistics about quality assurance and completeness for each monitor. More detailed information about quality assurance data is available in the Data Quality Indicators Report and more about completeness is available in the Data Completeness Report. Where the Certification report includes the same summary metric as one of the other reports, the values should match.
**Data Completeness**

Data completeness is based on the sample period start date and end date of the monitor and is not based on a calendar year. # 12 CFR § 620.3 - Accuracy of reports and assessment of internal control over financial reporting.
(a) Prohibition against incomplete, inaccurate, or misleading disclosures. No institution and no employee, officer, director, or nominee for director of the institution shall make any disclosure to shareholders or the general public concerning any matter required to be disclosed by this part that is incomplete, inaccurate, or misleading.
(c) Certification of financial accuracy. The report must be certified as financially accurate by the signatories to the report. If any signatory is unable to, or refuses to, certify the report, the institution must disclose the individual's name and position title and the reason(s) such individual is unable or refuses to certify the report. At a minimum, the certification must include a statement that:

(1) The signatories have reviewed the report,
(2) The report has been prepared in accordance with all applicable statutory or regulatory requirements, and
(3) The information is true, accurate, and complete to the best of signatories' knowledge and belief. If the report contains the limited disclosure authorized by § 628.62(c) of this chapter, the statement may be modified to explain that the completeness of the report was determined in consideration of § 628.62(c).

Copy link - The Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) has made it mandatory to obtain a satisfaction certificate from the ward councillor before processing payments for horticulture, development and drain and sewer-cleaning works, in a move aimed at strengthening oversight and accountability. Payment files for civic works will be processed further only after the councillor concerned submits a certificate confirming that the work has been completed satisfactorily, said officials. (HT Archive) In a separate order, municipal commissioner Dr Pankaj has also authorised ward councillors to physically verify the attendance of regular and outsourced sanitation workers deployed in their respective areas. Advertisement According to the first order, payment files for civic works will be processed further only after the councillor concerned submits a certificate confirming that the work has been completed satisfactorily. The measure is intended to ensure that payments correspond to work carried out on the ground and that contractors meet prescribed quality standards. The commissioner has directed additional commissioners, joint commissioners, the chief engineer, superintending engineers, executive engineers, assistant engineers and junior engineers to strictly implement the instructions while processing payment files in their respective zones and wards. Under the second order, councillors can conduct inspections during morning and evening shifts to verify whether sanitation workers are present at their designated locations and performing their assigned duties. The provision covers both regular municipal employees and outsourced sanitation staff.

**Author:** Tommie Singleton  
**Date Published:** 1 October 2014

So many times, auditors of all types use a computer-generated report to perform some aspect of assurance. For example, financial auditors may pull a computer-generated list of accounts receivable (i.e., subsidiary listing) and use it to confirm receivables. IT auditors sometimes do the same thing with lists of access, logs or other reports relevant to IT audits. A popular use today is to generate data sets (a similar resulting object) to conduct data mining or data analytics.

It is tempting to look at a neat report that came from a computer and to have a “leap of faith” as to the veracity and reliability of the information of that report. Standard setters have realized the fallacy of that thinking and have issued guidance to auditors regarding computer-generated reports. The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) inspection reports show that one major area of deficiency in financial audits of issuers is not gaining assurance regarding the accuracy and completeness of the report’s information.

## The Goal

The goal has been stated by standard setters. It is the completeness and accuracy of the information in the report upon which the auditor is relying. Accuracy alone is insufficient. One needs to obtain assurance about both the completeness and the accuracy.

The US Government Accountability Office (GAO) uses data reliability to refer to the accuracy and completeness of data. linkup.title: Reporting - Federation Council
linkup.snippet:
Council plans for our community, then reports on its implementation of these plans. Regular reporting takes place through the Annual Report, Delivery Program Progress Report (six monthly), Quarterly Budget Review Statement and Monthly Financial Performance Reports. In addition, Council provides an End of Term Report and conducts a Community Satisfaction Survey.  
Much of this reporting is a legislative requirement as part of the Local Government Act 1993 and provides a framework to enable Council internally to monitor and report against performance and provides Councillors and the community with a comprehensive overview of the progress and status of Council's performance.
Each year, individual local governments across New South Wales are required to present a set of audited financial statements to their Council and community.  
The Delivery Program Progress Report is a report from the general manager to the elected council.  
Council’s Quarterly Budget Review Statement provides a summary of council’s financial position to the elected council.  
Council’s Monthly Financial Performance Report provides a high-level summary of council’s financial position to the elected council.  
The End of Term Report covers the four-year term of the previous Council and tracks Council’s progress against the Community Strategic Plan (CSP).
Council’s Community Satisfaction Survey is conducted to understand and identify community priorities, to explore community experiences when contacting Council, and to measure overall satisfaction with Council's performance.  
The State of our Region Report covers the three-year term of the previous Council and tracks Council’s progress against the Community Strategic Plan (CSP).

## Summary

City staff told council the 2025 Consumer Confidence Report contained two reporting issues — omission of the word “free” before chlorine and a non-direct link to the Lead Service Line Inventory — both corrected after notice; council formally acknowledged completion of the report.

City Manager Rex M. Thee briefed the City Council on the 2025 Consumer Confidence Report for the City of Monahans’ public water system and opened a public participation opportunity on the report.

Mr. Thee told the council the report documents chemical analysis at multiple points in the system and described two reporting violations under Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) standards: \"the City did not use the word “free” in front of chlorine in the report,\" and the online Lead Service Line Inventory link \"took more than one click to reach i.e. was not a 'direct' link by TCEQ standards.\" Thee said both issues were immediately corrected upon notice. Council then voted unanimously to acknowledge completion of the 2025 Consumer Confidence Report.

The council’s acknowledgement is a procedural certification that the report was made available as required and that identified reporting deficiencies were fixed; no enforcement action or fines were announced at the meeting.

Victoria uses a different model: its Local Government Performance Reporting Framework is mandatory for Victorian councils and includes 59 service-area measures and a 27-item Governance and Management checklist.  ... Record the measure’s purpose, population or service boundary, reporting period, unit, direction of improvement and relationship to the relevant plan or obligation. State whether it measures an input, activity, output, service quality, outcome or impact. A count of completed inspections, for example, is not automatically evidence that risk has fallen; it may be an output that needs to be read alongside a quality or outcome measure.

The Australian National Audit Office’s guidance on meaningful performance information (https://www.anao.gov.au/work/insights/reporting-meaningful-performance-information) says measures should relate directly to purpose, be clear and logical, be complete and balanced, remain contemporary, and have an owner.  ... Note who can access the source, how often it is updated, whether it is authoritative for this purpose, and what happens when a value is corrected. ... Document the steps from source extract to reported figure: filters, joins, formulas, manual adjustments, aggregation, rounding and validation. For a manually entered value, record who supplied it, when, under what definition and who checked it. Where another organisation supplies data, record the agreed method and the checks performed before relying on it. ... Ask where the definition lives, who owns it, what source supports it, how the result is calculated, what exceptions occurred and what decision the report informs. The answers will show whether the main opportunity is clearer definitions, better hand-offs, stronger evidence records, more useful interpretation—or, only then, a technology change.

webiq.title: What Is Report Certification? Definition & Examples
webiq.snippet:
Report certification is the governance practice of formally validating that a report is accurate, reliable, and backed by traceable data sources. It relies on lineage, ownership, and transformation evidence so reviewers can confirm that the reporting chain is understood and controlled.

Report certification is not just sign-off on a finished document. It is the point where someone with ownership confirms the report can be trusted because its source data, transformations, and control checks are understood and defensible. ... webiq.title: Certification Records and Documentation Requirements
webiq.snippet:
ISO/IEC 17021-1, the internationally recognized standard for bodies providing audit and certification of management systems, defines specific record-keeping obligations in Section 9. These include requirements that records demonstrate competence of audit team members, document the basis for certification decisions, and capture any client-supplied information used in the assessment. Organizations pursuing management system certification under ISO 9001, ISO 14001, or ISO 45001 must expect their certification body to maintain this evidence portfolio independently of — and in addition to — the organization's own internal records.

The certification body holds audit reports, decision records, and complaint files as its own controlled documents. The certified organization maintains its internal quality management documentation, corrective action logs, and evidence of continued conformance.  ... - Application stage: The certification body records the client's application, scope request, and any pre-application communications. These establish the defined scope boundary against which all subsequent records are evaluated.
- Stage 1 audit documentation: For management system certification, a Stage 1 (document review) audit generates records confirming that the organization's documented system is sufficiently developed to proceed to Stage 2. Deficiencies noted at Stage 1 are recorded and tracked.
- Stage 2 audit records: Field audit records capture objective evidence — interviews, observations, document reviews — mapped against each applicable clause or requirement. Nonconformities are recorded with reference to specific clause numbers and supporting evidence.

ISO/IEC 17021-1 §9.5 requires that the decision be made by a person different from those who conducted the audit, and this separation must be documented.
- Certificate issuance record: The certificate number, scope, validity period, and issued-to entity are logged in the certification body's provider network.

webiq.title: What Is Completeness And Accuracy? Definition & Examples
webiq.snippet: Completeness is the scope test: whether the review data includes every item that should be present for the audit purpose. If records, cases, assets, or transactions are missing, the review output can look stronger than it really is. Completeness problems usually arise from incomplete source feeds, narrow extraction logic, or gaps in the review population. ... Accuracy is the correctness test: whether the review data reflects the real-world state at the time it is used. Even a fully populated dataset becomes misleading if fields are stale, misclassified, incorrectly entered, or no longer match the source of truth. ... *Recommendation — Review audit data for completeness, timeliness, and correctness before relying on conclusions. Reconcile the review population against authoritative account inventories. Use an authoritative inventory to confirm the review scope is complete.*
